title: Optimization of a Multiplex RNA-based Expression Assay Using Breast Cancer Archival Material
protocol: Prepare stained reference tissue sections using H&E procedures.
Digitally scan the slides for reference during microdissection.
Cut 20 μm tissue sections onto an RNAse-free water bath at 40 °C.
Collect the sections on membrane slides for laser microdissection using clean, RNase-decontaminated equipment and materials.
Dry the membrane slides at 37 °C in a drying incubator overnight.
Stain the membrane slides with H&E procedure with molecular biology grade solutions and increase the staining time of Hematoxylin to 6 min.
If required, stain the membrane slides with appropriate immunohistochemical protocols.
Set the slide limits and calibrate the stage movement for laser microdissection.
Move the laser view onto an empty area of a membrane slide.
Calibrate the laser focus by firing a laser shot at increasing focus intervals until the laser starts to pierce through the membrane.
Draw and microdissect any shape on the membrane slides.
Finetune the laser focus to maximize the laser efficiency during dissection.
Increase the stage movement speed to a point where the laser dissection efficiency is not compromised.
Calibrate the laser at the selected objective lens and re-calibrate if changing objectives.
Scan the stained membrane slides using the 4X objective.
Select and encircle the target areas for microdissection on the membrane slide.
Laser dissect a minimum area of 42 mm².
Record the area dissected to determine the volume of sample homogenizing buffer to be used.
Use the cap lift mechanism to retrieve the dissected section onto the diffuser caps of labeled tubes attached to the appropriate appendage.
Pipette 2.4 µL of homogenizing solution into each tube for each 1 mm² of tissue area.
Vortex for 10 s at maximum speed and centrifuge at room temperature for 5 s at 2,500 x g.
Incubate in a heating block at 65 °C for 12–18 h with shaking at 600 rpm.
Centrifuge the lysates at 21,000 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the clear supernatant using a pipette.
Dispense the aspirated supernatant into a labeled fresh tube.
Store the clear supernatant in a -80 °C freezer.
Pre-warm the lysis mixture by placing the reagent bottle in an incubator at 37 °C for 30 min.
Gently invert the pre-warmed lysis mixture to mix it.
Thaw frozen tissue homogenates at room temperature and then incubate them at 37 °C for 30 min.
Vortex the samples at maximum speed after incubation.
Set the shaking incubator at 54 °C.
Place the probe of the temperature validation kit in an empty well of a 96-well plate.
Check the temperature on the digital thermometer after 2 hours.
Correct the delta temperature setting of the shaking incubator based on any difference measured.
Thaw and vortex the probe set for 10 seconds.
Centrifuge the thawed probe set at room temperature for 5 seconds at 2,500 x g.
Keep the probe set and blocking reagent on ice during use.
Place the Proteinase K vial on ice during use.
Sonicate the capture beads at 46 KHz for 3 minutes.
Vortex the sonicated capture beads at maximum speed for another 3 minutes.

Prepare a 25 µL working bead mix per well by scaling up the following reagents accordingly: 4.25 µL of Nuclease-free water, 16.65 µL of lysis mixture, 1.00 µL of blocking reagent, 0.10 µL of Proteinase K, 0.50 µL of capture beads, and 2.50 µL of probe set.
Vortex the working bead mix for 10 s at maximum speed.
Pipette 25 µL of the working bead mix into each well of the magnetic separation plate.
Pipette 25 µL of tissue homogenate to a magnetic separation 96-well plate and 25 µL of homogenizing solution to 3 wells as blanks.
Seal the magnetic separation plate using a clear plastic pressure seal.
Place the sealed plate in the incubator at 54 ± 1 °C for 18–22 h while shaking at 600 rpm.
Mix 31.5 mL of RNase-free water with 0.1 mL of wash buffer component 1 and 1.67 mL of wash buffer component 2 to prepare a 1X wash buffer solution for 24 wells.
Remove the plate from the incubator after shaking at 50 ± 1 °C.
Mount the magnetic separation plate on the hand-held magnetic plate washer and lock in place.
Remove the pressure seal and wait 1 min for the magnetic beads to settle.
Invert the magnetic separation plate mounted onto the plate over the sink and blot gently on a tissue paper to remove residual solution.
Using a multichannel pipette, add 100 µL of 1X wash buffer solution into each well and wait 15 s.
Repeat this step two more times to wash the plate three times in total.
Pipette 50 µL of pre-amplifier reagent to each well.
Seal the plate with an aluminum plate seal.
Shake the plate at 800 rpm for 1 min at room temperature.
Incubate for 1 h at 50 ± 1 °C while shaking at 600 rpm.
Repeat step 4.9 (Washing step).
Pipette 50 µL of the amplifier reagent to each well.
Seal the plate with an aluminum plate seal.
Shake the plate.
Repeat step 4.9 (Washing step).
Vortex the label probe for 10 s at maximum speed.
Add 50 µL of the label probe to each well.
Seal and shake the plate.
Repeat Step 4.9 (Washing step).
Vortex the Streptavidin phycoerythrin (SAPE) for 10 s at maximum speed.
Add 50 µL of SAPE to each well.
Seal and shake the plate.
Repeat Step 4.9 (Washing step).
Use the SAPE wash buffer instead of the wash buffer solution.
Add 130 µL of SAPE wash buffer to each well.
Seal the plate with an aluminum plate seal.
Shake the plate at 800 rpm at room temperature for 3 min.
Start-up the magnetic bead analyzer.
Perform the calibration and verification routine by following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Set up a protocol on the magnetic bead analyzer using the following parameters: Sample Size: 100 µL; DD Gate: 5,000–25,000; Timeout: 90 s; Bead Event/Bead Region: 100.
Select the respective bead numbers in the panel and define the bead regions with the respective target genes as indicated by the manufacturer.
Add a new analysis by selecting “Create Batch using an existing protocol” from the Batches tab.
In the plate layout designate the wells as unknown or blank, respectively.
Provide a label for each sample in the Samples Panel.
Remove the aluminum plate seal from the 96-well reaction plate.
Eject the plate tray by clicking on the Eject button.
Load the plate into the magnetic bead analyzer.
Click Retract| Run Batch to initiate the analyzer.
After reading, eject and remove the 96-well plate.
Clean and shut down the magnetic bead analyzer as recommended by the manufacturer.
Select the respective analysis file in the Batch| Results tab.
Click the export to.csv button.
Open the.csv file using a spreadsheet software.
Observe the bead counts and omit any results with < 40 beads/region.
Average out the values of the blank wells.
Work out the standard deviation (SD) and Limit of Detection (LOD) (blank average + (3xSD)) per target gene.
Set the values lower than the LOD as undetected.
Subtract the blank average from the raw data per gene.
Compute the geometric mean of the selected normalizing genes per sample.
Normalize individual sample data to the respective geometric mean.
Import the data into the data science platform by clicking Add Data.
Drag the data file into the Process Workspace.
Connect to a Select Attributes operator.
Select the subset of normalized gene data and a nominal variable such as breast cancer subtype in the Select Attributes operator.
Connect from the Select Attributes operator to a Principal component analysis (PCA) operator.
Connect from the PCA operator to the result port.
Run the process by clicking Play.
In the Charts Tab, select “Scatter 3D Color” in the Chart style.
Select the nominal variable in the Color field.
Assess the PCA data variability on a 3-dimensional plot.
